entries.description: Convert Gaussian splats, such as posedImages2Splats returns, into a GLB mesh with an optional texture or vertex colors. Uses the project's World Labs Developer API credits. Returns an operation immediately; poll get_operation for the result. Reuse the same idempotency_key when retrying so the work is not submitted twice. Guide: https://docs.atlas.worldlabs.ai/api-reference/splats2-mesh.md

CamerasAutoAnchors.description:
Find anchor positions automatically, then render from them.

Candidates come from the free space the geometry encloses, and `oriented`
picks which rule judges one valid. The default when a request names no
cameras.

oriented.description: Judge a candidate by whether the surface faces it, which needs splats whose normals are oriented -- usually only true if they were optimized for it. Leave false to judge by enclosure alone, which is safe on any scene.
oriented.title: Oriented

CamerasAutoAnchors.title: CamerasAutoAnchors

CamerasExteriorSphere.description:
Render from a sphere around the splats, looking inward.

For anything whose surface can be seen from outside -- an object, a turntable
capture -- no anchors are needed. Cameras are spread evenly over a sphere
bounding the splats and aimed at its center. Naming an
`orientedBoundingBox` sizes that sphere on the splats inside it, which is
what picks one object out of a larger capture.
CamerasExteriorSphere.title: CamerasExteriorSphere

CamerasManualAnchors.description:
Render from explicitly placed anchor positions.

A cubemap is rendered at each anchor, and more cameras are sampled around
it. Anchors belong in open space, with a clear view of the regions that
matter most.

anchors.description: Anchor positions in Three.js coordinates (+X right, +Y up, -Z forward).
anchors.title: Anchors

CamerasManualAnchors.title: CamerasManualAnchors

CoordinateFrame.description:
Pose represented by a position and an XYZW quaternion.

``coordinate_system`` names the axes convention the pose is expressed in:
``rub`` (right-up-back, the OpenGL/Three.js convention) or ``rdf``
(right-down-forward, the OpenCV convention). Both the ``coordinateSystem``
(camelCase) and ``coordinate_system`` spellings are accepted.
CoordinateFrame.title: CoordinateFrame

PinholeCamera.description:
A posed pinhole camera.

The axes convention of the pose is carried by
``extrinsics.coordinate_system``.
PinholeCamera.title: PinholeCamera

PinholeCameraIntrinsics.description:
Pinhole camera intrinsics in pixel coordinates (not normalized).

Pixel coordinates have their origin (0, 0) at the top-left corner of the
image, +x right and +y down, so ``cx``/``cy`` measure from the top-left.
``width`` and ``height`` are the image size in pixels the intrinsics
refer to. This is independent of the pose's ``coordinate_system``.
PinholeCameraIntrinsics.title: PinholeCameraIntrinsics

Splats2MeshAdvancedOptions.description: Advanced reconstruction controls for custom mesh generation.

depthSource.description: Depth of the main views. `render` uses the splats' rendered depth; `stereo` measures it by stereo matching each view against a second render from a camera shifted sideways, which is sharper where the splats are fuzzy and slower to compute. Pixels stereo cannot match keep the rendered depth.
depthSource.title: Depthsource

normalSource.description: Normals orient the implicit surface the mesh is extracted from. `depth` estimates them from the rendered depth; `render` aggregates the splats' own, which assumes each splat's local z axis points along the surface normal.
normalSource.title: Normalsource

renderHw.description: Height and width of the main views rendered to measure the splat surface and texture it, in pixels.
renderHw.title: Renderhw

renderHwSecondary.description: Height and width of the secondary views, in pixels. The anchor strategies place extra cameras from the anchors and render them here, covering what the main views miss. `exterior_sphere` and a supplied camera list render no secondary views and ignore this.
renderHwSecondary.title: Renderhwsecondary

resolution.description: Resolution of the grid the implicit surface is built on, across the region's longest side. Powers of two only. This sets the finest detail the mesh can carry.
resolution.title: Resolution

trimQuantile.description: Drop vertices whose sample density falls below this quantile. Reconstruction closes the surface over regions it saw no samples in, and trimming cuts that invented skin back off. 0 keeps every vertex.
trimQuantile.title: Trimquantile

Splats2MeshAdvancedOptions.title: Splats2MeshAdvancedOptions

Splats2MeshColliderBoxOptions.description: Collider boxes to fit to the extracted mesh.

heightAlignVoxels.description: Tolerance, in voxels, for aligning heights: neighbouring box tops (and bottoms) within it of each other are raised to a shared height, so floors stay flat to walk on. A voxel is the mesh's longest side divided by `advancedOptions.resolution`. 0 keeps the fitted heights.
heightAlignVoxels.title: Heightalignvoxels

targetBoxes.description: Maximum number of boxes. Fewer boxes enclose the mesh more loosely.
targetBoxes.title: Targetboxes

Splats2MeshColliderBoxOptions.title: Splats2MeshColliderBoxOptions

Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox.description: Region to extract, as an oriented box in Three.js coordinates.

center.description: Center of the region, in world space.
center.title: Center

halfExtents.description: Half the region's size along each of its own axes. All three must be positive.
halfExtents.title: Halfextents

orientation.description: Rotation of the region away from the world axes, as an xyzw quaternion.
orientation.title: Orientation

Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox.title: Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox

TaskAsset.description:
Media named by asset id, inline base64, or public URL.

A task response names each output by id and url together: the url expires,
the id does not. The pair is accepted as input as well, so a response can
be handed straight back to the next task; the id names the media and the
url is ignored. Inline base64 stands alone. A response returns it only
when a task is answered at submission; the stored operation names the
same output by id and url.

base64.description: Base64-encoded media bytes, with or without a data URL prefix. Decoded size must be less than 10 MiB. A task response carries inline bytes only when it is returned from the submission; the stored operation names the same output by `assetId` and `url`.
base64.title: Base64

url.description: Public HTTP(S) URL containing the media. On a task response this is a read URL for `assetId` and it expires; mint a fresh one with `assets/{asset}:createReadUrl`.
url.title: Url

TaskAsset.title: TaskAsset

idempotency_key.description: A unique string you choose for this request and reuse on retries of it.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

advancedOptions.description: Finer control over how the splats are rendered and how the surface is extracted. Omit for the defaults.

cameras.description: Cameras the splats are rendered from. The surface is reconstructed from those renders, so geometry no camera sees is not meshed. Name a strategy -- `auto_anchors` (the default) finds viewpoints in the scene's free space, `manual_anchors` takes them from the request, `exterior_sphere` rings the scene from outside for an object or turntable capture -- or pass a list of cameras to render as given, at most 512, sharing one width and height between 64 and 1024 that becomes the render resolution.
cameras.title: Cameras

colliderBoxes.description: Also fit oriented boxes that enclose the mesh, for collision. The boxes stay upright, turning only about the vertical axis, and come back as a second GLB asset with one node per box. Omit to skip them.

orientedBoundingBox.description: Region to extract, as an oriented box in Three.js coordinates. Omit to mesh the whole scene.

purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.description: Purge this operation's outputs and the transient uploads it consumed one hour after it finishes. Omitted, the account's setting applies; true raises it for this operation; false is refused when the account already purges. Uploads in the library are never purged by an operation.
purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.title: Purgecontentonoperationcompletion

splatAsset.description: The Gaussian splat scene (.spz) to mesh. Inline base64 must carry a `data:` prefix to declare its media type: asset creation otherwise infers the type from the bytes, and the sniffer knows image formats only.

targetFaces.description: Decimate the extracted mesh to at most this many faces. A target above the extracted count does nothing. Omit to keep every face.
targetFaces.title: Targetfaces

textureMode.description: Mesh appearance: 'image_texture' projects rendered views onto a UV atlas, 'vertex_color' bakes per-vertex colors, and 'none' leaves the mesh untextured.
textureMode.title: Texturemode

textureSize.description: Height and width of the texture atlas, in pixels, for `image_texture` mode. One rendered view plus its border has to fit, so this must be at least 2% above the render size in play: the larger render bank under the anchor strategies, `renderHw` under `exterior_sphere`, or the supplied cameras' own size.
textureSize.title: Texturesize

webhookUrl.description: Where Atlas POSTs one signed task.succeeded or task.failed event when this operation finishes; retried for 24 hours. Verify the signature with the public keys at /.well-known/webhooks/jwks.json. Cannot be combined with ?wait=true. https on port 443 only, no IP literals. Developer API only.
webhookUrl.title: Webhookurl

The sources agree on the price tiers and on the free plan's export limit, but they disagree on which paid plan unlocks high-quality meshes and commercial rights.

**Plan prices:** Free is $0, Standard $20/mo, Pro $35/mo, and Max $95/mo, per a pricing comparison captured in November 2026 (World Labs plans and prices: Free $0, Standard $20, Pro $35, Max $95 per month).

**Free plan:** Free accounts can generate worlds but cannot export them (The Free plan can generate worlds but not export them.). One guide puts the free allowance at about four worlds (7,000 monthly credits, about four worlds, no card required.).

**Splat and mesh exports:**
- Splat exports: The official docs say the Standard plan covers SPZ and PLY splats, 360 panoramas, and collider meshes (Standard plan covers splat exports (SPZ and PLY), 360 panoramas, and collider meshes).
- High-quality mesh: The official docs tie the high-quality textured GLB mesh to Pro (High-quality textured mesh (GLB) export and commercial rights come with the Pro plan.). A third-party listing instead places high-resolution textured mesh export under Standard (Standard plan with 20,000 credits, export high-resolution textured meshes, commercial rights). I'd trust the official docs here.

**Commercial rights:** The billing documentation ties commercial rights to the Pro plan (World Labs' billing documentation ties commercial rights to generated worlds to the Pro plan.). The same third-party listing that puts commercial rights under Standard conflicts with this.

**API (separate from the app):** API billing is pay-as-you-go and separate from the Marble subscription. Credits cost $1.00 USD per 1,250 credits, with a minimum purchase of 6,250 credits or $5.00 USD. PLY splat exports through the API are free (PLY splat exports are free.). An HQ mesh export is billed as one event of 3,500 credits, about $2.80 (billed as a single HQ mesh export usage event of 3,500 credits ($2.80)).

**Bottom line:** Free users can't export. Standard covers splats and collider meshes. Pro is the tier to use for high-quality mesh and commercial use, though sources differ on that split, so check the live pricing page before committing.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

Nothing generated, nothing spent, no key used. Sources: official docs read 2026-11-16
(docs.worldlabs.ai/api, …/reference/worlds/get.md, …/worlds/list.md, …/worlds/export.md, …/api/pricing.md,
…/api/faq.md, …/marble/support/account-billing.md, docs.worldlabs.ai/llms-full.txt).

## Findings
| Route | Can it read a website-made world? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| claude.ai **World Labs Atlas** connector (connected; `list_projects` OK → "My project", credits available) | **No.** Atlas is a different product: its 11 tools generate images/depth/splats/meshes; none lists or opens Marble worlds | tool list in this session |
| **Marble World API** `GET https://api.worldlabs.ai/marble/v1/worlds/{world_id}` (header `WLT-Api-Key`) | **Unconfirmed.** Docs: "Only the world owner or users with access to public worlds can retrieve them." But the World endpoints "start generation jobs and manage worlds created through the API", and `worlds:list` "Returns worlds created through the API". Nothing says web-app worlds are included or excluded | get.md, list.md, llms-full.txt |
| Marble web-app export (marble.worldlabs.ai) | Yes, but **Free plan cannot export**; splats (SPZ/PLY) + collider mesh need Standard; HQ textured GLB needs Pro | marble export docs + pricing pages |
| Third-party "worldlabs-mcp" servers (e.g. github.com/sandraschi/worldlabs-mcp, glama listings) | Add no access: unofficial wrappers around the same World API, needing the same API key. Not installed | search 2026-11-16 |
| Pulling the splat files out of the web viewer's network traffic | Not done: it would bypass the export restriction | user rule |

## What a test would need (only with the user's go-ahead)
1. The world's ID (the part after `marble.worldlabs.ai/world/` in its URL).
2. A NEW World API key from platform.worldlabs.ai (signed in with the Marble login), given through the secure
   credential form for host `api.worldlabs.ai`, header `WLT-Api-Key` (never in chat or git). The account-7 key
   was exposed and must never be reused. The quickstart says to add a payment method and buy credits "to get
   started" (minimum US$5 = 6,250 credits); whether a key works for free read-only calls without a purchase is
   not stated. API billing is separate from the Marble subscription; Marble app credits cannot be used.
3. One `GET /marble/v1/worlds/{id}` (a read; not listed as a credit cost). If it returns the world, its
   `assets.splats.spz_urls` + `assets.mesh.collider_mesh_url` are already-generated files; PLY export is free
   (`POST …/worlds/{id}:export {"asset_type":"splats","format":"ply"}`); HQ mesh export = 3,500 credits (US$2.80),
   needs approval. If it returns 403/404, web-app worlds are not reachable by the API for this account.
4. Import with the existing credit-free tool `tools/blender/import_world_asset.py` (see `MARBLE_MANUAL.md`).

`qa/worldlabs/05/marble_user_world/vibrant_tunnel_of_fortune_screenshot.{webp,png}` (1366×555; original webp
SHA-256 `9f03860a…2a75`). The approved `references/05_flow_into_the_current.png` always takes priority.

content.text:
I've recovered your game on the new account without losing anything. Three specialists are now working on Screen 05's walls and rings, water, and foam. I can't reach your Marble world yet: that needs a new API key and the world's ID, and even then the docs don't confirm the API can read website-made worlds.

## Recovery
- **Branch:** I'm working on this session's branch, `ccr-4f6c3e0e-5kxgr0`. It contains the newest commit from `ccr-93add0fa-q17ey6` (`6cf0b4f`). Nothing was overwritten, and the backup and recovery branches are untouched.
- **Large files (Git LFS):** all 9 restored and verified (Benny and girl models, APK, Blender files, kit ZIP). The first download failed because of a leftover login setting; I cleared it and fixed the session-start hook so future sessions don't hit it.
- **Approved references:** all 12 images match their saved fingerprints.
- **Game:** the code compiles. The full gameplay test passes: coins, pause, heart loss, the 07→08 plunge (61.41) and the victory screen. There are no gaps between stages.
- **Tools:** all 10 specialist agents are present, Blender 5.3.0 is installed, and Playwright works. I haven't rebuilt the Android app this session yet; I'll do that with the final checks.
- **Backups:** I ran a manual backup and confirmed local and remote both at `42cab89`. Two things to know:
  - There were no backups from 00:02 to 00:37 UTC while the environment was closed during the account switch.
  - Your old account-7 session is still running and pushed an autosave to its own branch at 00:39. It only adds that session's transcript and no game code, but you may want to close it. I've added that branch to the protected list so this session's autosave can never push to it.

## Can I access your Marble world?
- **Atlas connector:** it is connected, but Atlas is a separate World Labs product. None of its tools can list or open Marble worlds.
- **Marble World API:** it can fetch a world by ID for "the world owner or users with access to public worlds". But the docs describe the world endpoints as managing "worlds created through the API", and they never say whether website-made worlds are included. Only a real test would settle it.
- **What that test needs:**
  - your world's ID (from its `marble.worldlabs.ai/world/…` link);
  - a new API key from platform.worldlabs.ai, entered through the secure form, never the exposed one.
  - **Possible cost:** the docs say to add a payment method and buy credits "to get started". The minimum purchase is $5, and it's separate from any Marble subscription. Whether a key works for free read-only calls without buying credits isn't stated.
- **If the API can read your world:** reading it isn't listed as a credit cost. It would return the splat files and collision mesh already made, and a .ply export is free. A high-quality mesh costs 3,500 credits ($2.80).

I saved your Marble screenshot in the repo as a secondary reference and sent it to the specialists. Your approved image stays the target.

2. **Washer walls (same specialist):** the swirly reflections are being replaced with clean violet-magenta metal, regular slot rows and lengthwise light streaks, using cues from your Marble world.
3. **Water and foam (water and foam specialists):** the flat vertical pink sheets and pool-like ripples become diagonal pink sweeps fanning from Benny, thick glossy cyan winding into the light, and low bubbly foam rims instead of white heaps.

The camera lock, river path, Benny, coins, HUD and gameplay are untouched. Each specialist must check screens 04, 06, 07 and 08 for regressions.

I've sent you image 1 (your approved Screen 05) and image 2 (the live game before changes). When the specialists finish, I'll send image 3 (after) at 864×1536 with a side-by-side and measured differences.

**Decision for you:** if you want the Marble test, send the world link and say whether you'll create a new key (which may require that $5 credit purchase). I'll then show the secure key form. Nothing else needs approval, and no credits have been spent.

Files are in `qa/worldlabs/05/MARBLE_ACCESS_2026-11-16.md` (Marble findings) and `qa/pilot05/COORDINATION_WAVE7.md` (Screen 05 plan).

List worlds with optional filters.

        - status: Filter by status (e.g., "COMPLETED")

        - is_public: Filter by visibility (true=public, false=private, null=all)

        - created_before: Filter by creation time (before timestamp)
        - sort_by: Sort order ("created_at" or "updated_at")

    ListWorldsResponse with worlds list and next_page_token for pagination.

                <CodeGroup>
                  ```bash Request theme={null}
                  curl -X POST 'https://api.worldlabs.ai/marble/v1/media-assets:prepare_upload' \

                    -H 'WLT-Api-Key: [REDACTED]' \
                    -d '{
                      "file_name": "my-image.jpg",
                      "kind": "image",
                      "extension": "jpg"
                  ```

                      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                      'WLT-Api-Key': '[REDACTED]'
                    body: JSON.stringify({
                      file_name: 'my-image.jpg',

                  ```

                  url = "https://api.worldlabs.ai/marble/v1/media-assets:prepare_upload"

                  ```

"""Marble World API pilot helper (Rainbow Screen 05). The API key is injected by the session proxy;
this script never reads, prints or stores it. Usage:
  marble_pilot.py credits
  marble_pilot.py upload <image.png>                 -> prints media_asset_id
  marble_pilot.py generate <model> <media_asset_id> <display_name> <prompt_file>  -> prints operation id
  marble_pilot.py poll <operation_id> <out.json> [max_seconds]
  marble_pilot.py world <world_id> <out.json>
  marble_pilot.py export_ply <world_id> <resolution> <out.json>
"""
import json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error

API = "https://api.worldlabs.ai/marble/v1"
CAP_SPEND = 6250          # user-approved maximum: US$5
START_BALANCE = 7000.0    # balance at the first authentication test (2026-11-16)


def call(method, path, body=None, timeout=60):
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    req = urllib.request.Request(API + path, data=data, method=method)
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read() or b"{}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        try:
            return e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"{}")
        except Exception:
            return e.code, {}


def credits():
    s, d = call("GET", "/credits")
    return d.get("remaining_credits") if s == 200 else None


def guard(cost):
    bal = credits()
    spent = START_BALANCE - bal
    if spent + cost > CAP_SPEND:
        sys.exit(f"REFUSED: spent {spent:.0f} + {cost} > cap {CAP_SPEND}")
    print(f"budget ok: balance {bal:.0f}, spent so far {spent:.0f}, this job ~{cost}, cap {CAP_SPEND}")


def main():
    cmd = sys.argv[1]
    if cmd == "credits":
        print(credits())
    elif cmd == "upload":
        path = sys.argv[2]
        ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lstrip(".").lower()
        s, d = call("POST", "/media-assets:prepare_upload",
                    {"file_name": os.path.basename(path), "kind": "image", "extension": ext})
        if s != 200:
            sys.exit(f"prepare_upload HTTP {s}: {d}")
        info = d["upload_info"]
        req = urllib.request.Request(info["upload_url"], data=open(path, "rb").read(),
                                     method=info.get("upload_method", "PUT"))
        for k, v in (info.get("required_headers") or {}).items():
            req.add_header(k, v)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
            print("upload HTTP", r.status)
        print("media_asset_id", d["media_asset"]["id"])
    elif cmd == "generate":
        model, asset, name, prompt_file = sys.argv[2:6]
        cost = {"marble-1.0-draft": 230, "marble-1.1": 1580, "marble-1.0": 1580}[model]
        guard(cost)
        body = {"display_name": name, "model": model,
                "world_prompt": {"type": "image", "is_pano": False,
                                 "image_prompt": {"source": "media_asset", "media_asset_id": asset},
                                 "text_prompt": open(prompt_file).read().strip()}}
        s, d = call("POST", "/worlds:generate", body)
        print("generate HTTP", s)
        print(json.dumps({k: d.get(k) for k in ("operation_id", "done", "error", "metadata")}, indent=1))
    elif cmd == "poll":
        op, out = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
        limit = float(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 540
        t0 = time.time()
        while True:
            s, d = call("GET", f"/operations/{op}")
            prog = (d.get("metadata") or {}).get("progress")
            if d.get("done") or s != 200 or time.time() - t0 > limit:
                break
            print(f"{time.time()-t0:5.0f}s {prog}", flush=True)
            time.sleep(15)
        json.dump(d, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
        print("HTTP", s, "done", d.get("done"), "error", d.get("error"))
    elif cmd == "world":
        s, d = call("GET", f"/worlds/{sys.argv[2]}")
        json.dump(d, open(sys.argv[3], "w"), indent=1)
        print("HTTP", s)
    elif cmd == "export_ply":
        wid, res, out = sys.argv[2:5]
        s, d = call("POST", f"/worlds/{wid}:export",
                    {"asset_type": "splats", "format": "ply", "resolution": res}, timeout=600)
        json.dump(d, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
        print("export HTTP", s, "done", d.get("done"), "error", d.get("error"))
    else:
        sys.exit(__doc__)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        print(credits())
    elif cmd == "upload":
        path = sys.argv[2]
        ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lstrip(".").lower()
        s, d = call("POST", "/media-assets:prepare_upload",
                    {"file_name": os.path.basename(path), "kind": "image", "extension": ext})
        if s != 200:
            sys.exit(f"prepare_upload HTTP {s}: {d}")
        info = d["upload_info"]
        req = urllib.request.Request(info["upload_url"], data=open(path, "rb").read(),
                                     method=info.get("upload_method", "PUT"))
        for k, v in (info.get("required_headers") or {}).items():
            req.add_header(k, v)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
            print("upload HTTP", r.status)
        print("media_asset_id", d["media_asset"]["id"])
    elif cmd == "generate":
        model, asset, name, prompt_file = sys.argv[2:6]
        cost = {"marble-1.0-draft": 230, "marble-1.1": 1580, "marble-1.0": 1580}[model]
        guard(cost)
        body = {"display_name": name, "model": model,
                "world_prompt": {"type": "image", "is_pano": False,
                                 "image_prompt": {"source": "media_asset", "media_asset_id": asset},
                                 "text_prompt": open(prompt_file).read().strip()}}
        s, d = call("POST", "/worlds:generate", body)
        print("generate HTTP", s)
        print(json.dumps({k: d.get(k) for k in ("operation_id", "done", "error", "metadata")}, indent=1))
    elif cmd == "poll":
        op, out = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
        limit = float(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 540
        t0 = time.time()
        while True:
            s, d = call("GET", f"/operations/{op}")
            prog = (d.get("metadata") or {}).get("progress")
            if d.get("done") or s != 200 or time.time() - t0 > limit:
                break
            print(f"{time.time()-t0:5.0f}s {prog}", flush=True)
            time.sleep(15)
        json.dump(d, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
        print("HTTP", s, "done", d.get("done"), "error", d.get("error"))
    elif cmd == "world":
        s, d = call("GET", f"/worlds/{sys.argv[2]}")
        json.dump(d, open(sys.argv[3], "w"), indent=1)
        print("HTTP", s)
    elif cmd == "export_ply":
        wid, res, out = sys.argv[2:5]
        s, d = call("POST", f"/worlds/{wid}:export",
                    {"asset_type": "splats", "format": "ply", "resolution": res}, timeout=600)
        json.dump(d, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
        print("export HTTP", s, "done", d.get("done"), "error", d.get("error"))
    else:
        sys.exit(__doc__)


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""Measure a Marble tunnel splat PLY: axis, wall radius, ring spacing, lids, river width, and an
unrolled wall image.  usage: analyze_splats.py <splats.ply> <out_dir>"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

ply, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
raw = open(ply, "rb").read()
hdr_end = raw.index(b"end_header\n") + len(b"end_header\n")
hdr = raw[:hdr_end].decode()
n = int([l for l in hdr.splitlines() if l.startswith("element vertex")][0].split()[-1])
props = [l.split()[-1] for l in hdr.splitlines() if l.startswith("property")]
a = np.frombuffer(raw, dtype="<f4", offset=hdr_end, count=n * len(props)).reshape(n, len(props))
P = {k: a[:, i] for i, k in enumerate(props)}
xyz = np.stack([P["x"], P["y"], P["z"]], 1).astype(np.float64)
rgb = np.clip(0.5 + 0.28209479 * np.stack([P["f_dc_0"], P["f_dc_1"], P["f_dc_2"]], 1), 0, 1)
alpha = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-P["opacity"]))
keep = alpha > 0.3
xyz, rgb = xyz[keep], rgb[keep]

# robust centre line: PCA on the points, axis = largest component, oriented away from the origin (camera)
c = np.median(xyz, 0)
u, s, vt = np.linalg.svd(xyz - c, full_matrices=False)
ax = vt[0]
if np.dot(ax, c) < 0:  # make +t point from the camera into the tunnel
    ax = -ax
t = (xyz - c) @ ax
# per-slice centre (the river makes the cloud asymmetric, so fit the centre per slice on the upper wall)
lo, hi = np.percentile(t, [1, 99])
bins = np.linspace(lo, hi, 61)
up_hint = np.array([0, 1, 0.0]) if abs(ax[1]) < 0.9 else np.array([1, 0, 0.0])
e1 = up_hint - ax * np.dot(up_hint, ax); e1 /= np.linalg.norm(e1)
e2 = np.cross(ax, e1)
d = xyz - c - np.outer(t, ax)
y1, y2 = d @ e1, d @ e2
r = np.hypot(y1, y2)
theta = np.arctan2(y2, y1)  # 0 = "up" hint direction
# camera-side "up": in Marble/OpenCV frames y is down; report both signs, pick wall = larger radius half
secs = []
for i in range(60):
    m = (t >= bins[i]) & (t < bins[i + 1])
    if m.sum() < 200:
        continue
    secs.append(dict(t=float((bins[i] + bins[i + 1]) / 2), n=int(m.sum()),
                     r_p50=float(np.median(r[m])), r_p90=float(np.percentile(r[m], 90))))
R = float(np.median([s_["r_p90"] for s_ in secs]))
wall = r > 0.75 * R

# gold = warm, bright, not pink:  R high, G mid-high, B low
R_, G_, B_ = rgb[:, 0], rgb[:, 1], rgb[:, 2]
gold = (R_ > 0.6) & (G_ > 0.35) & (B_ < 0.45) & (G_ > B_ + 0.12) & (R_ > G_)
cyan = (B_ > 0.6) & (G_ > 0.45) & (R_ < 0.45)
pink = (R_ > 0.65) & (B_ > 0.45) & (G_ < 0.4)
# rings: gold wall points histogram along t
gw = gold & wall
h, edges = np.histogram(t[gw], bins=400, range=(lo, hi))
hs = np.convolve(h, np.ones(3) / 3, mode="same")
peaks = [i for i in range(2, len(hs) - 2) if hs[i] == max(hs[i - 2:i + 3]) and hs[i] > 2.5 * np.median(hs[hs > 0])]
ring_t = [float((edges[i] + edges[i + 1]) / 2) for i in peaks]
spacing = np.diff(ring_t) if len(ring_t) > 1 else np.array([])

# river: cyan/pink points, lateral spread per slice
riv = cyan | pink
rw = []
for i in range(60):
    m = riv & (t >= bins[i]) & (t < bins[i + 1])
    if m.sum() > 100:
        lat = y2[m]
        rw.append(float(np.percentile(lat, 95) - np.percentile(lat, 5)))

# unrolled wall image: x = theta (-pi..pi), y = t (near at bottom)
W, H = 720, 1440
xi = ((theta[wall] + np.pi) / (2 * np.pi) * (W - 1)).astype(int)
yi = ((hi - t[wall]) / (hi - lo) * (H - 1)).clip(0, H - 1).astype(int)
acc = np.zeros((H, W, 3)); cnt = np.zeros((H, W))
np.add.at(acc, (yi, xi), rgb[wall]); np.add.at(cnt, (yi, xi), 1)
img = (acc / np.maximum(cnt, 1)[..., None] * 255).astype(np.uint8)
Image.fromarray(img).save(os.path.join(out, "wall_unrolled.png"))

res = dict(points_used=int(keep.sum()), axis=ax.tolist(), centre=c.tolist(),
           length=float(hi - lo), t_range=[float(lo), float(hi)], wall_radius_p90_median=R,
           sections=secs[::6], ring_t=ring_t, ring_spacing=spacing.tolist(),
           ring_spacing_median=float(np.median(spacing)) if len(spacing) else None,
           ring_spacing_over_radius=float(np.median(spacing) / R) if len(spacing) else None,
           river_width_p5_p95_median=float(np.median(rw)) if rw else None,
           river_width_over_diameter=float(np.median(rw) / (2 * R)) if rw else None,
           colour_fractions=dict(gold=float(gold.mean()), cyan=float(cyan.mean()), pink=float(pink.mean())),
           wall_mean_rgb=(rgb[wall & ~gold & ~cyan].mean(0) * 255).round().tolist())
json.dump(res, open(os.path.join(out, "splat_measure.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in res.items() if k not in ("sections",)}, indent=1))

"""Extract a hole-filled, physically proportioned wall texture for one bay (ring to ring) and the ring band
profile from a Marble tunnel splat PLY, using analyze_splats.py's measurements.
usage: bay_texture.py <splats.ply> <splat_measure.json> <out_dir>"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageFilter

ply, meas, out = sys.argv[1:4]
M = json.load(open(meas))
raw = open(ply, "rb").read()
he = raw.index(b"end_header\n") + 11
hdr = raw[:he].decode()
n = int([l for l in hdr.splitlines() if l.startswith("element vertex")][0].split()[-1])
props = [l.split()[-1] for l in hdr.splitlines() if l.startswith("property")]
a = np.frombuffer(raw, dtype="<f4", offset=he, count=n * len(props)).reshape(n, len(props))
P = {k: a[:, i] for i, k in enumerate(props)}
xyz = np.stack([P["x"], P["y"], P["z"]], 1).astype(np.float64)
rgb = np.clip(0.5 + 0.28209479 * np.stack([P["f_dc_0"], P["f_dc_1"], P["f_dc_2"]], 1), 0, 1)
alpha = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-P["opacity"]))
k = alpha > 0.3
xyz, rgb = xyz[k], rgb[k]
ax, c, R = np.array(M["axis"]), np.array(M["centre"]), M["wall_radius_p90_median"]
t = (xyz - c) @ ax
up = np.array([0, 1, 0.0]) if abs(ax[1]) < 0.9 else np.array([1, 0, 0.0])
e1 = up - ax * up.dot(ax); e1 /= np.linalg.norm(e1); e2 = np.cross(ax, e1)
d = xyz - c - np.outer(t, ax)
r = np.hypot(d @ e1, d @ e2); th = np.arctan2(d @ e2, d @ e1)
wall = (r > 0.75 * R) & (r < 1.4 * R)
rings = sorted(M["ring_t"])
gaps = [(rings[i], rings[i + 1]) for i in range(len(rings) - 1) if rings[i + 1] - rings[i] > 0.5 * (M["ring_spacing_median"] or 1)]
best = max(gaps, key=lambda g: ((t > g[0]) & (t < g[1]) & wall).sum())
sp = best[1] - best[0]
# texture spans one full spacing, centred on the bay, so the ring band sits on the top/bottom edges
t0, t1 = best[0], best[1]
W = 1024
H = int(round(W * sp / (2 * np.pi * R)))  # physical aspect: circumference x one ring spacing
H = max(64, H)
m = wall & (t >= t0) & (t <= t1)
xi = ((th[m] + np.pi) / (2 * np.pi) * (W - 1)).astype(int)
yi = ((t1 - t[m]) / (t1 - t0) * (H - 1)).astype(int)
acc = np.zeros((H, W, 3)); cnt = np.zeros((H, W))
np.add.at(acc, (yi, xi), rgb[m]); np.add.at(cnt, (yi, xi), 1)
cov = cnt > 0
img = acc / np.maximum(cnt, 1)[..., None]
# fill holes: repeated normalized blur of (colour*mask, mask)
filled = img.copy(); mask = cov.astype(float)
for rad in (1, 2, 4, 8):
    ci = Image.fromarray((filled * mask[..., None] * 255).astype(np.uint8)).filter(ImageFilter.BoxBlur(rad))
    mi = Image.fromarray((mask * 255).astype(np.uint8)).filter(ImageFilter.BoxBlur(rad))
    cb = np.asarray(ci).astype(float) / 255; mb = np.asarray(mi).astype(float) / 255
    hole = mask < 0.5
    est = cb / np.maximum(mb[..., None], 1e-3)
    filled[hole & (mb > 0.05)] = est[hole & (mb > 0.05)]
    mask = np.maximum(mask, (mb > 0.05).astype(float))
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
Image.fromarray((filled * 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(out, "bay_unrolled.png"))
Image.fromarray((cov * 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(out, "bay_coverage.png"))
# ring band profile: gold fraction vs t across +-0.3 spacing around each ring
gold = (rgb[:, 0] > 0.6) & (rgb[:, 1] > 0.35) & (rgb[:, 2] < 0.45) & (rgb[:, 1] > rgb[:, 2] + 0.12)
prof = []
for rt in rings:
    mm = wall & (np.abs(t - rt) < 0.3 * sp)
    if mm.sum() < 200:
        continue
    h_all, e = np.histogram(t[mm] - rt, bins=30, range=(-0.3 * sp, 0.3 * sp))
    h_g, _ = np.histogram(t[mm & gold] - rt, bins=e)
    frac = h_g / np.maximum(h_all, 1)
    band = (frac > 0.5)
    prof.append(dict(ring_t=rt, band_width=float(band.sum() * (e[1] - e[0])),
                     band_width_over_spacing=float(band.sum() * (e[1] - e[0]) / sp)))
res = dict(bay=[t0, t1], spacing=sp, texture_px=[W, H], coverage=float(cov.mean()), rings=prof,
           band_width_over_spacing_median=float(np.median([p["band_width_over_spacing"] for p in prof])) if prof else None)
json.dump(res, open(os.path.join(out, "bay_measure.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print(json.dumps(res, indent=1))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs headless Blender for Rainbow environment/character work (idempotent).
# Needs network access to download.blender.org (+ apt mirrors for libegl1).

set -euo pipefail
VER="${BLENDER_VERSION:-5.3.0}"
SERIES="${VER%.*}"
DEST=/opt/blender
if [ ! -x "$DEST/blender" ] || ! "$DEST/blender" --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "Blender $VER"; then

  (apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq libegl1 libsm6 libxi6 libxkbcommon0) > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
ln -sf "$DEST/blender" /usr/local/bin/blender
